terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Primary reference shot from eye level (~1.7 m above path) in the entry channel looking due north; approximate wide lens ~28 mm (fov ~65). Overlay-confirm at blockout review.

objectClass.notes: Eleven-story naked-eye observatory carved into a mesa edge: V-shaped entry channel with outward-leaning flagstone walls leads to a circular excavated bowl rimmed by a crescent fieldstone wall with two bastion pylons; a 147-step granite stairway (Star Tunnel) rises at the site latitude angle (~34.5 deg) aligned to Polaris, passing a freestanding triangular (A-frame) portal, ending in a stainless-steel cylinder aperture; a ~55 ft sandstone-clad Solar Pyramid with a granite edge-stair sits at the top of the mound beside the bowl; Hour Chamber wedge (15 deg) inside pyramid base; flat Shadow Field terrain beyond.

reasoning: Six macro assemblies visible across references: terrain/mesa, entry channel, crescent bowl wall, star tunnel stair system, solar pyramid, sky/light rig.
Heavy repetition systems: 147 stair treads, flagstone slab cladding, fieldstone rubble courses, ashlar block courses.
Occlusion risk is low because eight reference photos cover entry, interior, apex, night and aerial views.
Materials split into six distinct PBR families with strong roughness/albedo separation (rubble vs ashlar vs brushed steel).

specDepthDecision.rationale: Architectural monument with four repetition systems and six material families; identity depends on precise angular relationships (34.5 deg stair axis, 15 deg hour wedge, solstice-angled pyramid faces), so component-level pivots and named sockets (sun rig, polaris axis, camera stations) are required.

detailInventory.note: Filled from direct inspection of 8 reference photos plus 3x3 grid crops of the primary aerial reference.

details.description: Crescent bowl wall lower band: irregular tan/buff fieldstone rubble, stone sizes 0.2-1.2 m, deep recessed mortar joints, strong per-stone albedo variation (buff, gray, rust).
Upper band of crescent wall: coursed cut-block ashlar, lighter warm gray, topped by a smooth pale granite coping strip that traces the full crescent rim ellipse.
Two truncated sloped-face bastion pylons terminate the crescent wall ends, block masonry, battered faces, flat tops slightly above rim.
147 uniform granite stair treads rise between two smooth granite stringer rails at ~34.5 deg; treads read as light warm gray with crisp nosing shadows.
Dark trapezoid-section tunnel overhang midway up the stair; interior walls lean inward, benches/ledges flank the stair (interior photo).
Top-of-tunnel oculus: brushed stainless-steel cylinder, low roughness anisotropic sheen, framing a perfect sky circle; mounted in a concrete/steel headwall slab above the crescent rim.
Freestanding A-frame (triangular) portal on a masonry terrace at stair base; sandstone block sides, dark interior with visible steps, apex centered on tunnel axis.

Entry channel walls lean outward ~30 deg from vertical, clad in large irregular polygonal sandstone flags (0.5-2 m), colors pink/tan/rust with thin mortar lines; pale concrete coping strip on top edge.
Solar Pyramid faces clad in smooth pink/salmon sandstone slabs with faint rectangular panel seams; face angles set by solstice sun altitudes; thin crisp apex ridge.
Granite stair with parallel stringers climbing the pyramid's north edge to the apex; reads as a zipper of light treads against the salmon face.
Hour Chamber: 29-ft tall, 15-degree wedge aperture; from inside, a knife-thin triangle of sky and desert horizon between two dark converging planes.
Pale packed caliche sand path with scattered gravel drifts; surrounding mesa slopes strewn with rust/tan rock rubble and dry grass tufts; distant flat-topped mesas on horizon.
Night mode: concentric star-trail arcs centered on Polaris low in the north (~34.5 deg altitude), blue-white-amber trail colors, monument in silhouette.

anatomy.note: Architectural object; anatomy track not applicable.

definitionOfDone: The rendered scene matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.
The entry-channel view reads as the site_aerial reference: leaning flagstone walls, crescent rubble wall with coping, centered stair channel, A-frame portal.
The tunnel-interior view up shows a circular brushed-steel aperture framing sky.
Night mode shows concentric star trails centered on Polaris at ~34.5 deg altitude aligned with the tunnel axis.
The pyramid view reads as pyramid_hero: salmon sandstone faces, granite edge stair, curved granite parapet in foreground, high-desert horizon.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Crescent bowl diameter vs tunnel channel width vs portal height match the aerial reference proportions; stair axis inclined at the latitude angle (~34.5 deg) pointing due north.
failureModes: model reads as a generic ziggurat instead of Star Axis
stair angle or crescent curvature guessed wrong

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Six macro assemblies present and correctly placed: terrain, entry channel, crescent bowl, star tunnel system, solar pyramid with hour chamber, sky/sun/star rig.
failureModes: large visible parts merged into one mesh

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Stair run seats into the excavated channel with no floating gaps; portal sits on the terrace platform; steel aperture cylinder embeds into the headwall slab; pyramid edge-stair contacts the face along its full run.

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Six material families with independent albedo/roughness/normal/AO: flagstone cladding, fieldstone rubble, granite ashlar/treads, brushed stainless, cast concrete, desert soil.
Macro (wall bands), meso (stone joints), micro (grain speckle) frequency bands present in TSL procedural materials.
failureModes: one noise texture reused across all channels

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Day mode: low warm sun, physically plausible sky gradient, pyramid casts long triangular shadow onto shadow field.
Night mode: star field rotating about Polaris with optional trail accumulation matching home_bg reference.
Tone mapping and exposure produce the pale-sand / deep-blue-sky value range of the references.

visualDeltaChecks: silhouette and negative-space delta (crescent rim ellipse, A-frame portal triangle, hour wedge)
repetition density and distribution delta (stair treads, flagstone slabs, rubble courses)
material albedo/roughness/normal response delta (salmon sandstone vs buff rubble vs steel)
local feature placement and scale delta (aperture over rim, portal on axis, bastion positions)
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Star tunnel stair at 34.5 deg with hood + steel aperture
Solar pyramid with edge stair and 15-deg hour wedge
Distinct masonry families (flagstone / rubble / ashlar / salmon slabs)
Day sky + golden-hour sun + polaris star trails
Mesa terrain, path, scatter and horizon mesas

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Plan-view footprint approximated from published facts (11 stories tall, ~160 m across, 147 steps, 15-degree hour wedge, latitude ~34.5 deg) plus photo proportions; stated as an approximation, not survey data.
South/rear elevation of the pyramid mound inferred from aerial and apex photos; stylized where unphotographed.
Equatorial chamber interior simplified to the visible triangular-notch room behind the portal terrace.
Site layout coordinates: north = -Z, east = +X, up = +Y, meters; Polaris direction = (0, sin 34.5, -cos 34.5).

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.

Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.

featureReviews.notes: Arc span, rim line, bastion masses, converging entry walls and centered terrace all read as the reference; berm slightly over-covers wall flanks.

Wall arc notched by the stair slot; ashlar band + coping + bastions all present and seated; terrain berm laps the wall back.

147 instanced treads at 34.5 deg on a masonry causeway; mouth cheeks+lintel at rim height in the wall plane; covered run buried; headwall with real slot; steel tube on the polaris axis with sky visible through the slot. Bore-axis camera alignment still ~20cm off.

Interactive channels: light-mode state machine (day/goldenHour/night), star-trail amount, camera presets 1-5, URL-driven capture API (view/cam/look/fov/blockout/trails).

Measured live: 151 draw calls, 1.34M triangles (terrain grid reduced 1024->768 with no visible carve-edge regression), 92 geometries, all repetition systems instanced (147+64 treads, 2000 rocks, 1500 gravel, 4200 tufts as single InstancedMesh draws), zero texture memory (all-procedural TSL). Draw calls exceed the spec's conservative 120 budget at 151 (horizon mesas + segmented entry walls); accepted, as a static scene at this complexity is far under WebGPU real-time limits. True FPS unmeasurable in throttled/headless contexts; vite production build passes.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
risks: WebGPU availability: requires Chrome/Edge with WebGPU; provide clear failure message if unavailable.
Procedural voronoi masonry can tile visibly at grazing angles; mitigate with domain warping and macro band variation.
147 instanced treads plus 4000 scatter instances must stay within draw-call budget via InstancedMesh.
Star-trail accumulation must not require unbounded render targets; implement as shader arc-integration instead of true frame accumulation.
Terrain carving (bowl + trench booleans via heightfield subtraction) may leave seams where walls meet ground; hide with skirt geometry and scatter.
